courses.title: Children's Literature
courses.description: This course is a study of the literature of children (pre-elementary through young adult) with an emphasis on poetry, picture books, folk tales, myths, fiction, fantasy, and nonfiction from a variety of cultures, ethnicities, and historical periods. It also includes an evaluation of the literary quality and the cultural and historical meaning of individual works, and the study of the use of children's literature as an educational tool both in the classroom and outside of it.
courses.advisories: ENGL C1000 or ENGL C1000H or ESL D005.

courses.title: Introduction to Poetry
courses.description: The introductory poetry course is a critical and creative examination of the language and study of poetry through the lens of diverse perspectives, genres, and styles. Students will explore poetry ranging from classical to contemporary through global, historical, theoretical, and cultural vantage points. Through close examination of poetic devices, forms, and movements, the course invites students to engage in critical reading and writing skills focused on how poems produce meaning and why. The foundation of this course is the belief that poetry is one of the irreplaceable arts whose power and pleasure are open to all engaged students with an inclination to understand and savor them.

courses.title: Introduction to the Bible as Literature
courses.description: This is an introduction to the study of the Bible, in English, from a literary, cultural, and historical point of view, with consideration of its influence on our culture. Selected readings will be from the Hebrew Bible, Greek New Testament, and Apocrypha.
courses.advisories: ENGL C1000 or ENGL C1000H or ESL D005.

metadata.General Course Statement(s): (See general education pages for the requirements this course meets.)
metadata.Transferability: Transferable to both UC and CSU
metadata.Advisory(ies): ENGL C1000 or ENGL C1000H or ESL D005.
metadata.Student Learning Outcomes: Identify and analyze a range of literary expression in the Old and New Testaments and Apocrypha. Identify and analyze the stories and figures that are the basis for countless works of art, literary allusions, and philosophical constructs of the western tradition. Compare and contrast myth and narrative structures to other ancient Mediterranean and world literatures. Identify, articulate and apply a range of possible interpretations of selected texts. Demonstrate an understanding of trends in thought and in literary mode throughout the Bible.

courses.title: Mythology and Folklore
courses.description: This course is a comparative study of mythology and folklore from prehistoric, classical, and contemporary cultures around the world. It examines how myths and folktales reflect and shape a culture’s beliefs, values, art, and literature. Emphasis is placed on major mythological themes, archetypes, and symbols across diverse traditions and historical periods. Students will develop critical reading, writing, and analytical skills as they explore the continuing influence of mythology and folklore on literary and cultural expression.

courses.title: Asian American Literature
courses.description: This course is an introduction to Asian American literature. Through readings in twentieth and twenty-first century works, students will explore and analyze issues related to complexities of identity as it relates to class, gender, mixed heritages, and sexuality; politics and the history of Asian American activism and resistance to cultural marginalization; and diversity of cultures and experiences within the Asian American community.

courses.description: In this course students will examine critically texts of this genre, with particular attention to contemporary (postwar) dystopian novels, and with additional readings at instructor's discretion from political theory/philosophy, cultural studies, or other sources that foreground issues or themes implicit in the literary texts.

courses.title: World Literature: Africa and Latin America
courses.description: A comparative literature survey, "World Literature: Africa and Latin America" studies the works of literature of both Africa and Latin America from colonial times up to the present, in English and translation. The diversity of literature produced in both Northern and Sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America (including Brazil and the Caribbean), and various contemporary diasporas around the globe will be covered. The historically asynchronous approach investigates shared literary movements across national, linguistic, religious, and other social strata.

courses.student_learning_outcomes: Acquire knowledge of the historical and cultural period, major writers, and key texts and documents of American Literature from 1914 to present. Develop critical thinking skills by applying a variety of critical and theoretical criteria to the evaluation of American literature from 1914 to the present.

courses.title: Major American Writers (The Modern Age, 1914-the Present) - HONORS
courses.description: This course explores the reading and critical analysis of representative works by major writers of the modern and postmodern periods, such as Faulkner, Hemingway, Hurston, Morrison, Fitzgerald, Hughes, Wright, Ellison, Williams, Cisneros, Stevens, Sexton, Eliot, Vonnegut, Pynchon, O'Connor, Plath, Carver, Wilson, and O'Neill. Because this is an honors program course, students will be expected to complete extra assignments to gain deeper insight into English literature.
courses.prerequisites: Eligibility for college-level composition (ENGL C1000 or ENGL C1000H or ESL D005.) as determined by college assessment or other appropriate methods.
